title: Dimensional Change: Perimeter, Area, Surface Area and Volume
standard_text: G.10B determine and describe how changes in the linear dimensions of a shape affect its perimeter, area, surface area, or volume, including proportional and non-proportional dimensional change
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.10B: how scale factors change perimeter, area, surface area and volume, finding scale factors and non-proportional change. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Length × k, area × k², volume × k³.
key_sub: Double the radius of a sphere: volume × 8.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • If every length is multiplied by k: perimeter × k, area and surface area × k2, volume × k3.
  • If only some lengths change (non-proportional), multiply by the change in each length that appears in the formula.
  • From an area ratio, take the square root to get k; from a volume ratio, the cube root.

Examples

Example

A box with volume 40 cm³, scale factor 3

40 × 33 = 40 × 27

Answer: 1,080 cm³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying area by kArea uses k2.
Multiplying volume by k2Volume uses k3.
Doubling the volume when the radius doublesr is squared in V = πr²h.

items.q: Every length of a rectangular prism is multiplied by 10. What happens to its volume?
items.e: Volume is a cubic measure, so it is multiplied by (10)3 = 1,000.

items.q: A polygon has area 108 square units. It is dilated by a scale factor of 32. What is the area of the image?
items.e: Area is multiplied by the square of the scale factor: (32)² × 108 = 94 × 108 = 243 square units.

items.q: A polygon has area 7 square units. It is dilated by a scale factor of 5. What is the area of the image?
items.e: Area is multiplied by the square of the scale factor: (5)² × 7 = 25 × 7 = 175 square units.

items.q: A polygon has area 29 square units. It is dilated by a scale factor of 3. What is the area of the image?

items.q: A side of length 9 becomes 6 after a dilation. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = image ÷ original = 6 ÷ 9 = 23.

items.q: Two similar figures have corresponding sides in the ratio 4 : 7. What is the ratio of their areas?
items.e: The ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of sides: 4² : 7² = 16 : 49.
